piece.content_text:
Students at the National Institute for Zorig Chusum spend years mastering a single craft, thangka painting, wood carving, weaving, or one of ten other disciplines.

Zorig Chusum means Bhutan's thirteen traditional arts and crafts, and this government-run school in Thimphu exists for one clear purpose: to make sure those skills pass to the next generation rather than disappear. Each student follows a multi-year programme under experienced master craftspeople, which is why the standard of work inside is serious and deliberate.

There is a direct connection to the dzongs and monasteries families see elsewhere in Bhutan. The institute trains the artisans who restore and decorate those very buildings, so what looks like a separate stop starts to feel like a thread running through the whole journey.

For families, that context matters. Children can watch a discipline being learned at the same pace that craft has always demanded, and parents can see how Bhutanese cultural life holds together across centuries.

This visit sits within a broader morning in Thimphu. Message us to start planning your family trip.
